output.brief: The fall in incidents is not real. The platform's audit trail shows about 36 to 37 cases a month still reached confirmed-incident status, in line with the old roughly 38 a month. In total 47 of them (23 in September, 24 in October) were later switched to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring" by the Brackwater integration account. Each switch happened 3h31m to 3h42m after the case opened, just after the SLA warning flag. All 47 had analyst confirmation notes. They then dropped out of the containment and SLA figures, which is why containment looks like 100%. The monitoring queue grew from about 40 to about 96 cases. A vendor advisory describes a connector fault that overwrites categories after an SLA warning, and Corvane runs a version it names as affected. That fits the timing, but I can't rule out deliberate edits. The API gateway log (source host and user-agent) would settle it. Don't cut the IR retainer or pay the bonus now. Reinstate those cases, have your team and Halvard check containment on each, remove category-edit rights from the integration role, and ask Brackwater to explain in writing. Hold off on service credits until intent is known. Confidence: high that the fall is an artifact, moderate on the cause.
